name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 district lean in deep-red Alabama
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near zero
No polls or expert ratings; low-information race
model.rationale: A district that leans about 23 points Republican, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with under $10,000 on hand leave McInnis almost no plausible path. Markets price Rogers near certain, so the forecast sits at a deep Republican margin with only a token chance of an upset.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Rogers or a sudden influx of outside spending against him could put the seat in play; absent that, the race is unlikely to move.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent Mike Rogers is running again with a dominant financial position. He has raised about $2.1 million and holds $2.6 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Lee McInnis has raised roughly $61,000 with under $10,000 available. No general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets put Rogers' chances near certain.

The arithmetic is straightforward: a district that leaned roughly 23 points Republican at the presidential level, a heavily funded incumbent, and an opponent without the resources to introduce himself to voters. Even in a cycle when the national climate favors Democrats, the seat remains firmly in Republican hands. The forecast rates Rogers a heavy favorite, with any upset requiring an extraordinary and unforeseen shift in the race.
